subject: Response-time buckets and deployment mode — post-demo clarifications
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Lin <michael@stellarcheckout.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Response-time buckets and deployment mode — post-demo clarifications

Hey Michael / Tara —

Thanks again for the demo time today — appreciated the walkthrough of your checkout flow and the example traffic patterns. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we have a clear pilot plan: 

1) Need exact latency buckets (p50/p95/p99) for your real checkout calls and the QPS profile across a typical hour and peak 10-minute window. You mentioned the 9am holiday peak is the biggest pressure point — if you can share the 1-hour and 10-minute peak QPS that helps calibrate Dedicated capacity sizing.

2) For the pilot we recommended: start on Hosted API to validate correctness + integration, then exercise a burst-to-dedicated ramp for sustained peak windows. That gives you a fast path to production while keeping ops predictable.

3) Compliance note: you mentioned eventual VPC requirement for SOC2 evidence. We'll treat that as a near-term requirement for production and keep Private (VPC) as an option after pilot.

I've attached a short pilot MAP (redwood-pilot-MAP.docx) that lays out success criteria, benchmark ops, and the canary schedule. Can you confirm:
- 1-hour baseline QPS and 10-minute peak QPS numbers?
- p95/p99 targets you care about for request latency?
- Any hard limits on cold-start tail latency (e.g., >500ms seen is unacceptable)?

Proposed next steps: once we have the metrics we (Redwood) will propose a concrete pilot run window (2 weeks suggested) with a dedicated benchmarking slot to run against your representative traffic.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Karthik for the sizing once you share numbers.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: redwood-pilot-MAP.docx (outline of pilot milestones and runbook)
From: Michael Lin <michael@stellarcheckout.com>

Cc: Tara Gomez <tara.gomez@stellarcheckout.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 17:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Response-time buckets and deployment mode — post-demo clarifications

Hannah —

Great recap — thanks. Numbers below represent what we saw on last month’s run (non-holiday):
- Typical 1-hour baseline QPS (evening window): 45 qps
- 10-minute peak QPS (promo spike): 210 qps
- Peak sustained windows historically (Black Friday test): short bursts up to ~520 qps for 5-12 minutes

Latency (end-to-end for the checkout LLM call):
- p50: ~42 ms
- p95: ~162 ms
- p99: ~340 ms
- 99.9th: occasional 620-800 ms (we see these typically during burst cold paths)

Acceptable targets: p95 under 200ms is ideal, p99 under 400ms acceptable for now but we want to reduce the 99.9th to <500ms. If we see sustained >500 qps we will require a more predictable SLA (likely Dedicated).

Compliance: we have a SOC2 in progress; production will require VPC peering + audit log retention. For the pilot we're OK with Hosted provided logs are retained for 30 days and we sign a limited data handling addendum. I attached our SLA/req spreadsheet (stellar-sla-reqs.xlsx) for reference.

For the pilot, we prefer Hosted for the first 2 weeks to validate the integration and fallbacks. If Redwood can provide a short dedicated pilot ramp during the second week (so we can run a sustained 10–30 minute peak at ~400–520 qps), that will give us the confidence to commit.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m to align schedule.

Best,
Michael Lin
Head of Platform | StellarCheckout Inc.
michael@stellarcheckout.com | +1 617-555-0119

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Response-time buckets and deployment mode — post-demo clarifications

Thanks for the numbers, Michael — this is very helpful. Short summary from an ops/sizing perspective and proposed execution plan: 

Summary of signals:
- Baseline QPS small (45 qps), but short promotional spikes up to ~520 qps create tail latency risk.
- Target p95/p99 goals are achievable with batching and KV cache tuning; the 99.9th tail (600-800ms) needs targeted mitigations (warmup, prefetch, smaller cold-starts).

Recommended pilot approach (practical, low friction):
1) Week 1 (Hosted): Integration and correctness — validate prompts, tool-calls, and fallbacks against real traffic (replay 1-hour baseline + a single 10-minute spike at ~210 qps). Measure p50/p95/p99 and memory/KV cache behavior.
2) Week 2 (Hosted + Dedicated burst window): Keep the service on Hosted, but schedule a Dedicated bench window (we allocate a temporary Dedicated pool) to run two sustained 10–30 minute high-intensity tests at 400 qps and 520 qps. This isolates sustained-throughput behavior and validates routing/fallbacks.
3) Post-pilot: If Dedicated bench shows stable p95/p99 within targets and tail <500ms during the high-intensity tests, recommend moving to a Reserved Dedicated plan for production with a short VPC onboarding timeline (to satisfy SOC2).

Operational asks from Stellar for the pilot:
- Provide a 1-hour representative log + a 10-minute peak sample we can replay (we can accept a gzipped request log or a synthetic generator config).
- Confirm the acceptable maintenance window for the Dedicated bench (we prefer off-peak US hours, but can be flexible).

Technical nit: for the Dedicated bench we will provision a quantized model runtime tuned for throughput and enable prefix-caching for repeated prompt fragments — that should pull down p99 by ~20-30% in practice. We should also set the batching target to keep per-request latency under the p95 goal.

Next steps I’ll own: draft a concrete bench schedule and the runbook, share a HubSpot playbook link to the pilot record, and confirm the Dedicated bench availability. Hannah — can you propose two 60m slots next week for the kickoff call?

—
Karthik Iyer
